title: Conversation Fabric — feature sketch
content:
Context / one-liner:
A lightweight, modular "conversation fabric" layer that lets product teams compose conversational features from reusable "fibers" (context bundles, tool connectors, policy filters) so we can ship new flows without model-per-feature explosions.

Why this now:
- Increasing feature sprawl: we keep creating near-duplicate prompts and state logic across assistants.
- Cost & ops: each new flow currently risks new model config, rollouts, and eval overhead.
- UX reuse: many flows share canonical pieces (user profile, recent actions, task slot) that could be shared and cached.

Primary goals (MVP):
1) Define a first-class "fiber" primitive: small, serializable context piece with metadata (id, version, precedence, token-weight estimate).
2) Ingest/attach fibers at request time; runtime composes active fabric from route, user signals, and experiment flags.
3) Provide a simple DSL for ordering/merging fibers and a small SDK for product code to declare fibers (JS/TS prototype).
4) Prefix-level caching + KV hints so repeated fibers don't re-tokenize on every request.
5) Basic observability: token delta per fiber, hit/miss for cached fibers, and fiber-level error traces.

Success metrics (90 days):
- Developer velocity: time-to-prototype for new conversational microfeature down from ~4d to <1d (survey + PR time).
- Token savings: 10–20% average token reduction on targeted flows using fiber caching.
- De-dup: 30% fewer unique prompt templates for sampled product area.

User personas:
- Internally: product PM/PD building helper flows (quick prototypes).
- Internally: backend engineer responsible for rollout and observability.
- End-user: chat app user — seamless responses, faster replies, fewer hallucinations due to consistent context reuse.

MVP user stories (rough):
- As a PM, I can declare a fiber containing the "recent-actions" slot and attach it to a flow via a single route flag.
- As an engineer, I can mark a fiber as cacheable and see cache hit/miss in the console.
- As an SRE, I can configure fiber precedence rules so ephemeral debug fibers do not override production-critical fibers.
- As a data scientist, I can tag fibers with evaluation datasets to measure regression risk per fiber.

API sketch (prototype):
- Fiber schema (JS): { id, version, body, token_estimate, cacheable: bool, precedence: number, tags: [] }
- Compose: runtime.composeFibers([routeFibers, userFibers, experimentFibers]) -> ordered prefix string + metadata
- SDK: registerFiber(fiberDef) // server-side; attachFiberToRoute(routeId, fiberId) // product config

Runtime considerations / constraints:
- Tokenization cost: must expose token_estimate so router can make cost-aware decisions.
- Ordering: need deterministic merge semantics when multiple fibers provide same slot name. Precedence + last-write wins? canonical merge fn TBD.
- Size: fibers should be small (prefer <256 tokens) — but some may be template-heavy. Consider indirect references (store large fiber in object store + reference id).
- Backward compatibility: support existing prompt templates as fibers (adapter layer).

Observability & safety:
- Expose fiber-level token delta and per-request fiber list in traces.
- On eval regression, ability to toggle fiber off per customer/route.
- Fiber tagging for PII-sensitive content (KMS/HSM guardrails at private deployments).

Rollout plan (phased):
1) Prototype: local JS/TS SDK + runtime adapter that concatenates fibers and returns debug metadata (2 weeks).
2) Internal dogfood: enable for a small set of internal routes (help center assistant, admin tools). Measure token delta, dev time (4 weeks).
3) Beta: expose 'fibers' feature flag in console and allow product routes to opt-in. Add cache and observability (6–8 weeks).
4) Public: docs/SDK release + examples and migration path for existing templates (follow-on).

Open questions / risks (notes to self):
- Who owns fiber catalog? product team or infra? Need governance + naming conventions.
- Can we make token_estimate accurate enough for routing? maybe use simple tokenizer-based estimate on registration + sample-run calibration.
- How to handle fiber versioning for rollbacks across customers without creating combinatorial explosion? consider per-customer pinning and automatic fallback to a default fiber version.
- Interaction with model rollouts: switching model must preserve fabric semantics. Provide automatic regressions detector that runs evals per fiber.
- Security: fibers may include user-identifiable summaries — ensure private deployments honor retention and redaction policies.

Quick prototype TODOs (next 7 days):
- [ ] Wire up a registerFiber API stub in the local SDK (Rowan)
- [ ] Build a toy console page to attach fiber to a route (Mika)
- [ ] Add token_estimate util in tokenizer service (Devon)
- [ ] Create a simple cache key proto and add cache metrics to tracing (Evelyn)
- [ ] Draft short internal playbook: how to convert templates -> fibers (share with PMs)

Notes & heuristics (freeform):
- "Fibers" should be composable like CSS classes, not monolithic prompt blocks. Encourage small, single-responsibility fibers.
- Think about "fiber transforms": small functions that can post-process fiber body (redact, normalize). Could live as first-class micro-functions with permissions.
- For private deployments, allow a local fiber store with stricter retention.

References / inspiration:
- Modular config systems (CSS/Tailwind for prompts).
- Feature flags + middleware chaining patterns.
- Prior art: "session-templates" notes in drive, but this is intentionally focused on runtime composition and fiber cataloging.

Parking-lot ideas (future):
- Fiber marketplace: curated, versioned fibers that teams can adopt with telemetry.
- Fiber-level A/B testing (swap fiber variants in routing).
- Visual fiber composer in Console (drag-drop ordering) — later piece once model semantics settle.

---
End quick sketch. This is me thinking out loud; will refine after prototype feedback.
